The debugger sees the pull-up, drives the line low for TDeb0, the UPDI starts its clock and holds the line low for TUPDI until the clock is stable, then releases it high. The debugger must send the start bit of the first SYNCH within TDebZ max, or the UPDI turns off and the sequence starts again.

A high-voltage pulse on the RESET pin switches it to UPDI whatever RSTPINCFG says. Steps: reset the device first (recommended), apply the HV pulse, send the NVMPROG key after the first SYNCH, and when done write UPDIDIS in UPDI.CTRLB with STCS. The power-on reset must have been released before the pulse; the pulse should last 100 µs to 1 ms before the pin is tri-stated. The rising edge of the pulse resets the UPDI, which stays in reset after tri-stating until the debugger drives RESET low; the fuse enable sequence then follows. Once enabled by HV, only a POR returns the pin to its fused function; UPDIDIS resets the UPDI and drops its clock request but leaves the pin as UPDI. An ESD pulse on a poorly protected pin can act as an HV enable. The HV threshold depends on VDD.

operation.topic: RESET pin as GPIO and HV enable
operation.text: With RSTPINCFG at 0x0 the RESET pin is a GPIO. Its output driver stays off for at least 8.8 ms after a system reset so that it cannot fight an HV enable sequence. A system reset before entering HV programming is recommended.

During start-up the UPDI turns itself off and drops its power-management requests on a time-out (no SYNCH within 16.4 ms at a 4 MHz UPDI clock after it releases the pin; it counts 65536 UPDI clock cycles) or on a bad SYNCH (too long for its baud register, or too short to resolve). A new enable sequence is then needed. A session ends by writing UPDIDIS in UPDI.CTRLB: the UPDI issues a system reset (the CPU comes back running), drops its clock request and clears its keys and settings. Without that the UPDI and its oscillator request stay on and the supply current stays higher.

The UPDI detects parity, contention and frame errors and access time-outs; PESIG in UPDI.STATUSB holds the error signature. On an error it enters an error state and ignores everything but a BREAK. To recover: send a BREAK, send a SYNCH at the wanted rate, read PESIG with LDCS; the UPDI is then ready for the next SYNCH and instruction.

operation.topic: UPDI direction change and guard time
operation.text: When turning from receive to transmit the UPDI inserts idle bits (the guard time, set by GTVAL in UPDI.CTRLA, each bit at the current baud rate) before the first response byte. The guard time is the least idle time the debugger sees; the longest is the time-out; synchronisation plus bus access can make it longer than the guard time. The recommended setting is a guard time of two or more bits from the UPDI and one bit from the debugger.
All instructions are one byte, each preceded by a SYNCH. They reach the UPDI's own control and status (CS) space and the memory-mapped system space.

Direct-address loads and stores, address and data each up to 32 bits. LDS: after the opcode the programmer sends Size A address bytes and the data comes back after the guard time; with REPEAT the address is sent again for every repetition (no auto-increment). STS: address bytes, an ACK from the UPDI, then Size B data bytes and a second ACK. The synchroniser between DL and ACC layers adds a delay before read data appears.

Indirect loads and stores through the UPDI pointer, address and data up to 32 bits, with optional post-increment for use with REPEAT. The pointer is written with ST and Ptr = 0x2 (Size A address bytes, then ACK) and can be read back with LD. Data is then written with ST and Ptr = 0x0 (or 0x1 to step the pointer by the data size after each write), Size B data bytes, then ACK; LD returns data after the guard time. With REPEAT, set the start address once and use post-increment; data blocks of Size B may follow each ACK.

Byte-only access to the UPDI control/status space, the address carried in the instruction. LDCS returns one byte after the guard time. STCS is followed directly by its data byte and gives no response.

Loads the repeat counter; the next instruction runs RPT_0 + 1 times (once when the counter is 0), up to 255 repeats, and only its first issue needs SYNCH and opcode. Any instruction but REPEAT can be repeated; only a BREAK stops a repeat. LD with REPEAT streams data continuously after one guard time. With LD/ST use pointer post-increment, or every repetition hits the same address; LDS/STS need their address each time.

Sends a key (64 bits only) to unlock protected features, or reads the System Information Block (up to 128 bits). Size C sets the number of bytes. A key gets no response; the SIB comes back after the guard time.

operation.topic: Flash CRC at boot via UPDI
operation.text: The Flash CRC check run at boot works on a locked device too; its result is read from ASI_CRC_STATUS.

The UPDI SYNCH event can be routed through the event system to a TCB in input capture frequency measurement mode (CNTMODE = 0x3, CAPTEI = 1, EDGE = 0) to measure the system clock. A slow SYNCH rate, 10-50 kbps, gives a better count; the first capture is discarded and the second used. At 10 kbps the capture window is 200 µs. The count can be read from TCBn.CCMP after the SYNCH.
In multi-byte reads (LD with REPEAT, SIB readout) bytes follow with no guard time. Setting IBDLY in UPDI.CTRLA inserts two idle bits between bytes to give the debugger time to sample.
The SIB can be read at any time, whatever the lock bits, as ASCII. A 16-byte KEY read with SIB set returns it all; an 8-byte read returns the Family_ID only.

Send the Chip Erase key; optionally check CHIPERASE in UPDI.ASI_KEY_STATUS; write the RSTREQ signature to UPDI.ASI_RESET_REQ (system reset), then write 0x00 to it; poll LOCKSTATUS in UPDI.ASI_SYS_STATUS until it reads 0; ERASE_FAILED = 0 there means success. The lock bits are then clear and the UPDI has full access; until then only CS-space operations work. The BOD is forced on during chip erase at the level set by FUSE.BODCFG and BOD.CTRLB; with VDD below it the device stays unavailable until VDD rises.

Writing the NVM while the CPU runs gives unpredictable execution, so: chip erase if locked; send the NVMPROG key (optionally check it in the key status); write the RSTREQ signature to UPDI.ASI_RESET_REQ, then 0x00; wait for NVMPROG = 1 in UPDI.ASI_SYS_STATUS; write the NVM through the UPDI; write the RSTREQ signature and then 0x00 again to finish.

operation.topic: UPDI user row programming on a locked device
operation.text: Send the USERROW-Write key (optionally check UROWWRITE); reset through UPDI.ASI_RESET_REQ (signature, then 0x00); wait for UROWPROG = 1 in UPDI.ASI_SYS_STATUS; write the data into the first 32 bytes of RAM (writes elsewhere are not done, and the RAM cannot be read back in this mode), mapping one to one onto the user row; set UROWDONE in UPDI.ASI_SYS_CTRLA; wait for UROWPROG = 0; write UROWWRITE in UPDI.ASI_KEY_STATUS; reset through UPDI.ASI_RESET_REQ again.

The UPDI PHY runs in every sleep mode and stays reachable. In a mode that stops the system clock it cannot reach the bus, so when enabled it requests the system clock: CLKREQ in UPDI.ASI_SYS_CTRLA, 1 by default while the UPDI is on, keeps the clock running and emulates sleep so registers stay readable even in the deepest mode. INSLEEP in UPDI.ASI_SYS_STATUS shows whether the system domain is asleep.
The CPU runs the AVRxt version of the AVR instruction set.

An ideal n-bit single-ended ADC maps GND to VREF linearly onto 2^n codes of 1 LSb, from 0 to 2^n - 1. Offset error: how far the first transition (0x000 to 0x001) sits from its ideal place at 0.5 LSb. Gain error: with offset removed, how far the last transition (0x3FE to 0x3FF for 10 bits) sits from its ideal place 1.5 LSb below full scale. INL: with offset and gain removed, the largest distance of any transition from its ideal place. DNL: the largest departure of a code width from 1 LSb. Quantization error: always ±0.5 LSb. Absolute accuracy: the largest distance of any unadjusted transition from its ideal place, all the errors above together; ideal ±0.5 LSb. The ideal value of offset, gain, INL and DNL is 0 LSb.
Typical values are at T = 25 °C and VDD = 3 V unless stated; minimum and maximum values hold over the operating temperature and voltage range unless stated.
Silicon errata for the ATtiny1614/1616/1617 are published in Microchip document DS80000886.
